fields.label: H2
lines: Salt, Sunlight and Twenty Years Outdoors
fields.value: Salt, Sunlight and Twenty Years Outdoors
fields.note: 6 words · the three conditions that decide compound choice in this sector. A vehicle or a vessel is an outdoor structure with a long service life, and that is closer to a facade than to a factory

fields.label: Intro
paragraphs: Rolling stock and vessels are outdoor assets with thirty-year lives, washed regularly and exposed continuously. Seals fail by ozone cracking, UV embrittlement and salt attack long before they reach a temperature limit. Every compound we mix is available; these are ranked for transport duty.
fields.note: 45 words · same mechanism-first framing as the construction sheet, because the failure mode is the same one. “Washed regularly” is the sector-specific addition — detergent and high-pressure washing is a real ageing input on both trains and ships, and almost nobody mentions it

fields.label: Compound router
rows: External sealing — windows, doors, hatches, gangways
The default for anything exposed. Outstanding ozone, UV and water resistance; tested to ISO 1431-1. Never where oil or fuel is present
Salt air, moderate oil, flame-retardant grades wanted together
The classic marine and rail compromise, and the reason it appears in six of the eight applications above
Buffers, stops, acoustic and vibration pads
Best damping and flex-fatigue of the eight. Protected positions only — poor ozone resistance
Oil, fuel, hydraulic fluid, bilge duty
Engine room and oil-contaminated positions. Never on an external seal — nitrile has poor ozone resistance and crazes in sunlight
High-temperature gasketing, exhaust and boiler positions
Where temperature genuinely governs. Low tear strength, so not for a section stretched over a frame
Internal and protected positions only. No exposure, no oil
Aggressive chemistry, fuel systems, hot hydrocarbons
Specify on the medium, not the temperature
Hot oil and oil mist above nitrile’s ceiling
Engine-bay positions. The middle answer between NBR and FKM
fields.note:
Every range is the homepage compound table, which governs across all fifteen category pages. FKM and AEM carry the continuous figure beneath the peak.
Neoprene ranks second here and nowhere else in the set. That is the sixth distinct ranking across the six compound routers written in this run — EPDM-then-medium on diaphragms, natural rubber on bonded components and lining, NBR on seals, EPDM on construction, EPDM-then-neoprene here. Six pages, six orders, ranked on duty rather than on margin
🛑 “Flame-retardant grades” in the neoprene row is a compound property and must never be written as a fire rating. EN 45545-2 classification is a tested result on a specific material — see section 06

sections.title: Where we sit in the supply chain
sections.chip: 🛑 New · the section that defines the page
sections.live: NO LIVE SECTION → prose plus table · this is the section the sector needs and the one a buyer will screenshot

fields.label: H2
lines: We Supply the Builder, Not the Railway
fields.value: We Supply the Builder, Not the Railway
fields.note: 7 words · the clearest sentence in the whole content set. It is the page’s entire commercial position, it is true, and it converts a limitation into a defined role. A buyer who reads only this heading has understood the offer correctly

fields.label: Body
paragraphs: Rail and marine are approval-gated sectors. Supplying rubber components directly into an Indian Railways project requires RDSO vendor approval for the item; supplying into a classification society’s surveyed scope requires type approval from that society. We hold neither, and we will not imply otherwise. What we do is supply the builders, integrators and shipyards who hold their own approvals and buy components made to their own drawings — which is most of the rubber on a train or a vessel, and all of it in non-safety-critical positions.
leads: We hold neither, and we will not imply otherwise.
fields.note: 85 words · the extractable answer for this page. It names both gates, states the position, and immediately reframes it as a defined role rather than an absence. “Which is most of the rubber on a train” is true and it is the sentence that keeps the enquiry alive

fields.label: Scope table
rows: Window, door, gangway, hatch and porthole seals to the builder’s drawing
Acoustic and thermal insulation cut to the builder’s development
Gaskets, grommets and vibration mounts for auxiliary and services positions
Aftermarket and MRO supply for privately operated fleets
Export supply where the OEM holds the approval
fields.note:
Five and five, side by side, in one table. Reading down the right column tells a buyer in ten seconds whether to stop, and the left column tells them what is still worth an enquiry. That is a faster qualification than any form
The fourth right-hand row is the one that matters most technically. Brake, suspension and stern tube seals are where a rubber failure is a safety event, and they are exactly the parts a general rubber supplier is most tempted to quote. Naming them removes the temptation from both sides
Seventh boundary section in seven new sheets — and the only one where the boundary is commercial rather than technical. Diaphragms refused cycle life, bonded components refused bond strength, lining refused polyurethane and butyl, seals refused polyurethane, the datasheet refused food contact and a flame rating, construction refused bridge bearings. Here the refusal is about who Margo is allowed to sell to

notes: The body paragraph is this page’s extractable answer. Written to stand alone in an AI response to “does Margo Rubber supply Indian Railways”. That the answer is no, stated by us, is the outcome we want — a wrong yes from an assistant costs a qualification cycle.

sections.title: Technical & commercial questions
sections.live: NO LIVE SECTION → FAQ accordion, six questions · these six are the FAQPage mainEntity, verbatim

fields.label: Q1

parts.text: No. RDSO vendor approval is item-specific and we do not hold it, so we cannot supply rubber components directly into an Indian Railways project. We supply rolling stock builders, integrators and private fleet operators who buy to their own drawings under their own approvals. If your enquiry is for an RDSO-gated item, we will tell you at enquiry rather than at qualification.

fields.note: 64 words · the first question on the page, because it is the first question in the buyer’s head. Answering it before anything else is what makes the other five credible. The last clause is the commercial argument — a supplier who declines early is a supplier worth keeping on file

fields.label: Q2

lines: Can you supply material classified to EN 45545-2?

parts.text: Not as classified material. EN 45545-2 hazard levels — HL1, HL2 and HL3 — are tested classifications covering flame spread, ignitability, heat release, smoke opacity and toxicity, awarded on a specific material by a testing house. We hold no classification. We do supply flame-retardant neoprene grades where a specification asks for a compound property, and we will arrange third-party testing on request. We will not describe a flame-retardant compound as EN 45545 compliant.
parts.lead: We will not describe a flame-retardant compound as EN 45545 compliant.

fields.note: 75 words · the same structure as the construction sheet’s fire answer and deliberately so — two industry pages giving the same answer to the same class of question in the same voice is a house position. Naming the five tested parameters shows the refusal is informed rather than reflexive

fields.label: Q3

lines: Do you have class society type approval for marine components?

parts.text: No — not from DNV, Lloyd’s Register, ABS, Bureau Veritas, ClassNK or the Indian Register of Shipping. Components inside a surveyed hull or machinery scope need type approval from the vessel’s society and we hold none. We supply shipyards and marine equipment builders for accommodation, interior and auxiliary positions outside that scope, made to their drawing.

fields.note: 57 words · names all six societies rather than saying “class approval”, because a buyer searches the society name. A named absence is checkable; a vague one reads as evasion

fields.label: Q4

lines: Which rubber lasts longest on an external vehicle seal?

parts.text: EPDM. Rolling stock and vessels are outdoor assets with thirty-year lives, washed regularly and exposed continuously, and seals fail by ozone cracking and UV embrittlement rather than by reaching a temperature limit. Neoprene is the answer where salt air, some oil and a flame-retardant grade are wanted together. Nitrile is the common cheap substitute on external positions and it crazes within a season in sunlight.

fields.note: 66 words · the technical answer that earns the page its keep, and it is the same mechanism the construction sheet explains for facades. The nitrile warning appears on both pages because the mistake is made on both sectors

fields.label: Q5

lines: Can you make a non-standard section for our door or hatch?

parts.text: Yes — that is most of what we do on this sector. Dies are cut in-house, so a section drawn for your vehicle is a drawing rather than a compromise, and corner mouldings can be vulcanised to the profile so the joint is not a butt splice on assembly. Send the section drawing and the annual metreage and we will quote the die with it.

fields.note: 65 words · the qualifying answer for a builder, and the vulcanised-corner detail is what separates a component maker from a stockist on both this sector and construction

fields.label: Q6

lines: What is the minimum order for a build programme?

parts.text: We deal in bulk, and this sector buys both ways on one purchase order. Extruded profile is quoted per section against total length; moulded components carry the standard minimum of 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound, or are quoted against the part where tooling makes that unrealistic. Send the drawing package with the build quantity and we will price it as a package.

fields.note: 64 words · the bulk position adapted to a sector that buys metres and pieces together, matching sheets 18, 38 and 41. “Price it as a package” is the right commercial answer for a builder issuing a drawing set rather than a part enquiry
